title: POC weekly deployment readout — observability & gateway sync
summary: Weekly sync to review POC onboarding progress, gate provisioning, and a discrepancy seen in tail latency on Wednesday's load test. Agreement to run a narrow microbench (cold vs warm KV cache) and to finalize SSO/KMS handoff steps. Redwood will deliver telemetry dashboard link and narrowbench script; customer to provide SAML export and firewall egress rules.
next_steps: Redwood to share narrowbench script + telemetry dashboard link by 2025-05-02
Customer to provide SAML metadata and a test user by 2025-05-05
Run microbench (cold vs warm KV) and upload raw results by 2025-05-06
action_items: Lina to upload telemetry dashboard link and narrowbench script — due 2025-05-02
Marco to run cluster-side KV warm/cold microbench and attach logs — due 2025-05-06
Priya to provision SSO test user and share SAML cert — due 2025-05-05
Samir to provide current firewall/NAT egress rules for gateway — due 2025-05-04
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-04-30 09:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Lina Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (BrightScale), Priya Nair (BrightScale), Samir Desai (BrightScale)

Summary (auto): quick status, one anomaly in tail latency, gating on SSO/KMS and a small microbench to isolate KV cache behavior.

00:00:00 Lina: hey everyone, good morning, thanks for joining. we have about 38 minutes so i'll try to keep this tight. quick roll call?
00:00:08 Jared: Jared here, hey.
00:00:10 Priya: Priya on my side.
00:00:11 Samir: Samir, yeah.
00:00:13 Marco: Marco from Redwood, se on the call.
00:00:17 Lina: great. first item, onboarding progress — Priya, any blockers with gateway creds or env access since last week?
00:00:26 Priya: yeah, two small things. the gateway provisioning hit a snag with our egress rules. the NAT is blocking the health checks from the redwood endpoint, i think because the ip changed after the burst test.
00:00:40 Lina: okay, that's in line with what we saw in the logs. Marco, do you want to summarize the health-check pattern?
00:00:45 Marco: sure. so the gateway does a short-lived TLS handshake and then an auth token exchange, we rely on outbound to a couple of endpoints, sometimes the ip ranges rotate if you're on cloud provider, um, so if there's strict NAT with no egress allow-list, checks drop. we can provide a small egress list or use a static proxy.
00:01:03 Priya: static proxy is preferable for us, but we'll try opening the ranges first. Samir, any SRE comments?
00:01:09 Samir: yeah, we can add the ranges for now. jen's off today so i'll put it in the firewall rule change and test this afternoon.
00:01:15 Lina: perfect. next up — observability and the weird tail latency we saw on Wednesday. Marco, can you walk through the bench results?
00:01:23 Marco: yeah, quick recap. we ran the 10k token burst sim and aggregate p50/p95 looked good, p99 spiked to ~420ms which is about 3x expected. initial suspicion was garbage collection on the host, but looking at the telemetry the spike correlates with a cold KV cache miss pattern — so the KV lookup path added extra disk reads.
00:01:48 Jared: cold K V? are you saying the key-value cache wasn't warmed? we thought the prefix caching would handle that.
00:01:55 Marco: right, so prefix cache warms for common prefixes but our micro-sim has a spread of conversation starters so some shards never warmed the k-v (we saw K V spelled out in telemetry), then the runtime had to fetch from backing store which is slower.
00:02:08 Priya: do we have the exact time window? can we correlate to app traffic?
00:02:12 Marco: yes, i'll attach the raw CSV, but roughly 09:12 to 09:18 UTC we saw the highest error/latency. there was also a small spike in i/o wait on the node.
00:02:24 Samir: is there a known mitigation? pre-warm script?
00:02:27 Marco: we have a couple options — increase prefix length for caching, pre-warm via a background job (we can provide a narrowbench script that exactly reproduces warm vs cold cases), or configure an in-memory k-v tier. each has cost/latency tradeoffs.
00:02:42 Lina: sounds like the microbench is the agreed next investigative step. i'll share the script.
00:02:47 Jared: fine. another question — on telemetry, some of the labels in the dashboard don't match our internal naming, eg., "request_owner" shows as redwood_user sometimes, it's confusing.
00:02:58 Marco: ah yeah that's our standardized tag mapping — we can add a config mapping so the labels match your naming.
00:03:04 Priya: that would help for alerting.
00:03:06 Marco: we'll add mapping and share the updated dashboard link.
00:03:10 Lina: good. next — SSO/KMS handoff. Priya, you were going to share SAML metadata?
00:03:17 Priya: yes, we're almost ready. question on KMS: the docs mention Redwood supporting HSM-backed keys; do we need custom integration? our security team wants all keys in our cloud KMS.
00:03:29 Marco: we support customer-managed KMS via standard provider integrations (ez, we call it K M S) — you can either have us call your KMS via delegated role or we can accept wrapped keys. for on-prem HSM it's a slightly different flow. for the POC, delegated role is easiest.
00:03:45 Priya: okay we prefer delegated roles. i'll get security to produce the role and the service account.
00:03:51 Samir: also firewall — are there any inbound ports we need to open?
00:03:55 Lina: no inbound from internet; the gateway initiates outbound. we only need the egress holes Marco described.
00:04:01 Samir: cool.
00:04:05 Jared: small product question — if we scale to 2x concurrency, does caching behavior change? i've seen different batching behavior in other vendors like VeloxAI where they force bigger batches.
00:04:15 Marco: Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching with adaptive sizing, so at higher concurrency you do get larger batches which amortize kernel cost. caching still behaves the same, but warm cache is more effective since more requests hit same prefixes.
00:04:29 Jared: makes sense.
00:04:32 Lina: ok let's capture explicit next steps. Marco, you'll ship the narrowbench and raw csv instructions.
00:04:38 Marco: yes, i'll post a small script and a runbook for cold vs warm runs.
00:04:42 Priya: i'll provision the SAML test user and share cert by monday.
00:04:46 Samir: i'll update firewall by end of day and ping once health checks pass.
00:04:51 Lina: and i'll share the telemetry dashboard link with mapping and an example alert rule.
00:04:56 Jared: one more minor item — pricing question for dedicated vs hosted if we go beyond pilot. can we get an indicative quote?
00:05:03 Lina: yes we can share a ballpark; i'll send a simple sheet after this call.
00:05:07 Priya: thanks.
00:05:09 --- midcall note --- the team ran through a quick live check on gateway handshake (not recorded here) and verified a transient cert mismatch that Samir will remediate.
00:22:15 Marco: returning to telemetry — we noticed some mis-tagged endpoints where the model name shows as "model-unknown" in traces, likely from old agent versions. that may hide model-level regressions.
00:22:26 Lina: is that a config we can flip?
00:22:28 Marco: yes, it's a small agent env var. we'll include it in the dashboard update.
00:22:32 Priya: great.
00:30:10 Jared: circling back to SLA — we need to ensure p99 <= 200ms for our interactive feature. is that realistic on hosted or do we need dedicated?
00:30:20 Marco: depends on request size and quantization. for your 512 token median it's achievable on hosted with pinned capacity; if you need true isolation and predictable tail, dedicated gives better guarantees. we'll include recommendations in the follow-up.
00:30:34 Lina: ok, action list recap: Lina share dashboard + price sheet; Marco share narrowbench + runbook + raw csv; Priya share SAML + test user; Samir share firewall rules. timeline: everything to start rolling early next week, bench results by 2025-05-06.
00:30:58 Jared: sounds good. thanks everyone.
00:31:02 Priya: thanks.
00:31:03 Samir: thanks, goodbye.
00:31:05 Marco: thanks, bye.
00:31:07 Lina: bye all.

End of recording. Notes: several mis-transcriptions likely in agent labels (K V vs KV), timestamps approximate. Attachments to follow: narrowbench script, telemetry dashboard link, raw CSV instructions.
